questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

When we went to the cinema, the film __**already started**__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "had already started."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The past perfect tense **"had already started"** is the correct form to use in this sentence.
 
• It indicates that the film had already started before the time of the past event (when we went to the cinema).
 
• In this sentence,** "had already started"** is the correct past perfect tense to indicate that the action (the film starting) occurred before another past action (going to the cinema).
 
• The correct answer is option 1.

 

**Correct sentence**: *When we went to the cinema, the film **had already started.**__*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 4, "was already start"**, is missing the auxiliary verb "had" and is in the present tense instead of the past.
 
• **Option 2, "has started"**, is in the present perfect tense and implies that the film is still currently playing.
 
• **Option 3, "would already start"**, is a conditional tense and does not fit the context of the sentence. It implies that the film would have already started if a certain condition had been met.

questions.question:
**Direction: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

options.text: He goes to Shimla every year

questions.solution:
Here, the erroneous part is **"he was going to Goa."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part **"he was going to Goa."**
 
• The sentence is in the past tense, so the correct form of the verb **'go' **would be **'went.'**
 
• The error is in the use of the present continuous tense 'he was going', which is not appropriate for a completed action in the past.
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

 

**Correct sentence**: *He goes to Shimla every year but this year **he went to Goa**__.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

**__Between the 11 members of the team__**, there was great discord and this led to their dismal performance.

options.text: Between the 11 member off the team
Among the 11 members of the team
Between the 11 members in the team
Beside the 11 members of the team

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Among the 11 members of the team."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Between"** is used when there are only two things or people being compared.

 
 
• **Example**:* There is no comparison **between**__ Rahul and Riya.*
 
 
 
• In this case, there are 11 members, so we need to use **"among"** instead.
 
• **"Among"** is used when there are three or more things or people being compared.
 __
 
• **Example**: *There is no comparison among__ them.*
 
 
 
• Using **"between"** in this sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The word **"off"** is not necessary and would make the sentence incorrect if used.
 
• **"Beside"** means next to or alongside, so it does not make sense in this context.
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.

**Correct sentence**: *__**Among the 11 members of the team**__, there was great discord and this led to their dismal performance.*
